solution:
Using the vector triple product identity \(\vec{x}\times(\vec{y}\times\vec{z}) = (\vec{x}\cdot\vec{z})\vec{y} - (\vec{x}\cdot\vec{y})\vec{z}\):
\(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}\)
\(\vec{b}\times(\vec{c}\times\vec{a}) = (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a})\vec{c} - (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{a}\)
\(\vec{c}\times(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}) = (\vec{c}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{a} - (\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a})\vec{b}\)
Adding all three and grouping by \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}\):
\(\big[(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})-(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a})\big]\vec{b} + \big[(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{b})-(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\big]\vec{a} + \big[(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a})-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\big]\vec{c}\)
Since the dot product is commutative (\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=\vec{c}\cdot\vec{a}\), etc.), each bracket is \(0\).
\(\therefore \vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) + \vec{b}\times(\vec{c}\times\vec{a}) + \vec{c}\times(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}) = \vec{0}\) — Hence proved.

Let \(\vec{a}=3\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+5\hat{k},\ \vec{b}=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k},\ \vec{c}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) be the co-terminus edges.
Volume of parallelepiped \(= |[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]|\)
\([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = 3\big(2\times4-(-3)\times1\big) - 0\big(4\times4-(-3)\times3\big) + 5\big(4\times1-2\times3\big)\)
\(= 3(11) - 0 + 5(-2) = 33-10 = 23\)
\(\therefore\) Volume \(= |23| = \mathbf{23}\) cubic units.

Vectors \(-3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k},\ \hat{i}+2\hat{k},\ \hat{i}-p\hat{j}\) are coplanar \(\Rightarrow\) their scalar triple product is \(0\).
\(-3\big(0\times0-2\times(-p)\big) - 4\big(1\times0-2\times1\big) + (-2)\big(1\times(-p)-0\times1\big) = 0\)
\(-3(2p) - 4(-2) - 2(-p) = 0\)
\(-6p + 8 + 2p = 0\)
\(-4p = -8\)
\(\therefore p = \mathbf{2}\)

Write \(\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c} = \vec{a}+(\vec{b}+\vec{c})\), so by linearity of the scalar triple product in the third slot:
\([\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}] = [\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}] + [\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}]\)
In the first term the 1st and 3rd vectors are both \(\vec{a}\); in the second term the 2nd and 3rd vectors are both \(\vec{b}+\vec{c}\). A scalar triple product with two equal vectors is always \(0\).
\(\therefore [\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}] = 0+0 = \mathbf{0}\) — Hence proved.

Write \(\vec{a}+2\vec{b}-\vec{c},\ \vec{a}-\vec{b},\ \vec{a}-\vec{b}-\vec{c}\) as linear combinations of \(\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}\); their coefficients form the matrix (rows = the three vectors, columns = coefficients of \(\vec a,\vec b,\vec c\)):
\(M=\begin{pmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\ 1 & -1 & 0\\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{pmatrix}\)
By multilinearity of the scalar triple product, \([\vec{a}+2\vec{b}-\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}-\vec{b}\ \ \vec{a}-\vec{b}-\vec{c}] = \det(M)\,[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)
\(\det(M) = 1\big((-1)(-1)-0(-1)\big) - 2\big(1(-1)-0(1)\big) + (-1)\big(1(-1)-(-1)(1)\big)\)
\(= 1(1) - 2(-1) - 1(0) = 1+2-0 = 3\)
\(\therefore [\vec{a}+2\vec{b}-\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}-\vec{b}\ \ \vec{a}-\vec{b}-\vec{c}] = 3[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) — Hence proved.

Given \(\vec{c}=3\vec{a}-2\vec{b}\).
By linearity of the scalar triple product in the third slot:
\([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = [\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}\ \ 3\vec{a}-2\vec{b}] = 3[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{a}] - 2[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{b}]\)
Both \([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{a}]\) and \([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{b}]\) are \(0\), since each has a repeated vector.
\(\therefore [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = 3(0) - 2(0) = \mathbf{0}\) — Hence proved.
(This is consistent with the given condition \([\vec{a}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}]=0\), which in fact holds identically for any \(\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}\) — see Q.4(i).)

Here \(\vec{u}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k},\ \vec{v}=3\hat{i}+\hat{k},\ \vec{w}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
Using the identity \((\vec{p}\times\vec{q})\times(\vec{q}\times\vec{r}) = [\vec{p}\ \vec{q}\ \vec{r}]\,\vec{q} - [\vec{q}\ \vec{q}\ \vec{r}]\,\vec{p} = [\vec{p}\ \vec{q}\ \vec{r}]\,\vec{q}\) (since \([\vec{q}\ \vec{q}\ \vec{r}]=0\)), with \(\vec p=\vec u,\vec q=\vec v,\vec r=\vec w\):
\((\vec{u}\times\vec{v})\times(\vec{v}\times\vec{w}) = [\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}]\,\vec{v}\)
\([\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}] = 1(0\times(-1)-1\times1) - (-2)(3\times(-1)-1\times0) + 1(3\times1-0\times0) = -1-6+3 = -4\)
So \((\vec{u}\times\vec{v})\times(\vec{v}\times\vec{w}) = -4\vec{v} = -12\hat{i}-4\hat{k}\)
Also \(\vec{u}+\vec{w} = \hat{i}-\hat{j}+0\hat{k}\)
\((\vec{u}+\vec{w})\cdot\big[(\vec{u}\times\vec{v})\times(\vec{v}\times\vec{w})\big] = (\hat{i}-\hat{j})\cdot(-12\hat{i}-4\hat{k}) = -12+0+0 = \mathbf{-12}\)

Using the identity \([\vec{u}\times\vec{v}\ \ \vec{u}\times\vec{w}\ \ \vec{v}\times\vec{w}] = [\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}]^2\):
From part (i), \([\vec{u}\ \vec{v}\ \vec{w}] = -4\)
\(\therefore [\vec{u}\times\vec{v}\ \ \vec{u}\times\vec{w}\ \ \vec{v}\times\vec{w}] = (-4)^2 = \mathbf{16}\)

Volume of tetrahedron \(= \dfrac{1}{6}\big|[\vec{AB}\ \vec{AC}\ \vec{AD}]\big|\)
\(\vec{AB}=B-A=4\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-2\hat{k},\ \ \vec{AC}=C-A=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+0\hat{k},\ \ \vec{AD}=D-A=0\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
\([\vec{AB}\ \vec{AC}\ \vec{AD}] = 4\big((-1)(1)-(0)(-4)\big) - (-4)\big((3)(1)-(0)(0)\big) + (-2)\big((3)(-4)-(-1)(0)\big)\)
\(= 4(-1) + 4(3) - 2(-12) = -4+12+24 = 32\)
\(\therefore\) Volume \(= \dfrac{1}{6}|32| = \mathbf{\dfrac{16}{3}}\) cubic units.

Here \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k},\ \vec{b}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k},\ \vec{c}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
\(\vec{b}\times\vec{c} = \hat{i}(2\times3-1\times1) - \hat{j}(3\times3-1\times2) + \hat{k}(3\times1-2\times2) = 5\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = \hat{i}(2\times(-1)-3\times(-7)) - \hat{j}(1\times(-1)-3\times5) + \hat{k}(1\times(-7)-2\times5) = 19\hat{i}+16\hat{j}-17\hat{k}\)
Now \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} = 2+2+9=13\) and \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=3+4+3=10\)
\((\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c} = 13(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}) - 10(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) = 19\hat{i}+16\hat{j}-17\hat{k}\)
Both sides equal \(19\hat{i}+16\hat{j}-17\hat{k}\) — Hence \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b}-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}\) is verified.

Here \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j},\ \vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j},\ \vec{c}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
\(\vec{b}\times\vec{c} = \hat{i}(2\times(-2)-0\times1) - \hat{j}(1\times(-2)-0\times2) + \hat{k}(1\times1-2\times2) = -4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = \hat{i}((-2)(-3)-0(2)) - \hat{j}((1)(-3)-0(-4)) + \hat{k}((1)(2)-(-2)(-4))\)
\(= \mathbf{6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k}}\)

\(\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \hat{i}((-2)(0)-0(2)) - \hat{j}((1)(0)-0(1)) + \hat{k}((1)(2)-(-2)(1)) = 4\hat{k}\)
\((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c} = 4\hat{k}\times(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}) = 8(\hat{k}\times\hat{i}) + 4(\hat{k}\times\hat{j}) - 8(\hat{k}\times\hat{k})\)
\(= 8\hat{j} - 4\hat{i} - 0 = \mathbf{-4\hat{i}+8\hat{j}}\)
Comparing with part (i): \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = 6\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-6\hat{k}\) but \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c} = -4\hat{i}+8\hat{j}\) — the results are **not** the same.
Justification: cross product is not associative in general. Using \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})=(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b}-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}\) and \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}=(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b}-(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{a}\), here \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}=0,\ \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=-3,\ \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=4\), so the two expressions reduce to \(3\vec{c}\) and \(-4\vec{a}\) respectively — unequal since \(3\vec{c}\) is not a scalar multiple of \(\vec a\) here. Equality would require \((\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}=(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{a}\), which does not hold for these vectors.

\(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\) is a vector, so the dot product \(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\) is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a scalar** (this is the scalar triple product \([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)).

\(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\) is a scalar. The cross product \(\vec{a}\times(\text{scalar})\) is **not defined**, since the cross product is defined only between two vectors.
**Not meaningful.**

\(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\) is a vector, so \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\) (a vector triple product) is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a vector.**

\(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\) is a scalar. The dot product \(\vec{a}\cdot(\text{scalar})\) is **not defined**, since the dot product requires two vectors.
**Not meaningful.**

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}\) are both scalars. The cross product between two scalars is **not defined**.
**Not meaningful.**

\(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\times\vec{d}\) are both vectors, so their dot product is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a scalar.**

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\) is a scalar. \((\text{scalar})\cdot\vec{c}\) is **not defined**, since the dot product needs two vectors.
**Not meaningful.**

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\) is a scalar, and multiplying a scalar with the vector \(\vec{c}\) is ordinary scalar multiplication, which is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a vector.**

\(|\vec{a}|\) and \(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\) are both scalars, and the product of two scalars is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a scalar.**

\(\vec{b}+\vec{c}\) is a vector, so \(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}+\vec{c})\) is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a scalar.**

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\) is a scalar and \(\vec{c}\) is a vector. Adding a scalar and a vector is **not defined**.
**Not meaningful.**

\(|\vec{a}|\) is a scalar and \(\vec{b}+\vec{c}\) is a vector; multiplying a scalar with a vector is ordinary scalar multiplication, which is defined.
**Meaningful — it is a vector.**

Volume \(V(a) = 1\big(1\times1-a\times0\big) - a\big(0\times1-a\times a\big) + 1\big(0\times0-1\times a\big) = 1 + a^3 - a\)
Differentiating: \(\dfrac{dV}{da} = 3a^2-1\)
For extremum: \(3a^2-1=0 \Rightarrow a^2=\dfrac13 \Rightarrow a=\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\)
\(\dfrac{d^2V}{da^2} = 6a\)
At \(a=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\): \(\dfrac{d^2V}{da^2}>0 \Rightarrow\) minimum. At \(a=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\): \(\dfrac{d^2V}{da^2}<0 \Rightarrow\) maximum.
\(\therefore\) Volume is minimum at \(\mathbf{a=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}}\), the minimum value being \(1-\dfrac{2}{3\sqrt3} = 1-\dfrac{2\sqrt3}{9}\).

Place the cube with one vertex at the origin \(O\), edges of length \(a\) along the axes, so the adjacent vertices are \(P(a,0,0), Q(0,a,0), R(0,0,a)\).
The three face diagonals meeting at \(O\) are:
\(\vec{d_1} = \vec{OP}+\vec{OQ} = a\hat{i}+a\hat{j}\) (diagonal of the face \(z=0\))
\(\vec{d_2} = \vec{OQ}+\vec{OR} = a\hat{j}+a\hat{k}\) (diagonal of the face \(x=0\))
\(\vec{d_3} = \vec{OR}+\vec{OP} = a\hat{i}+a\hat{k}\) (diagonal of the face \(y=0\))
Volume \(= |[\vec{d_1}\ \vec{d_2}\ \vec{d_3}]| = \big|a(a\times a-a\times0) - a(0\times a-a\times a) + 0\big| = |a^3+a^3|\)
\(\therefore\) Volume of the parallelepiped \(= \mathbf{2a^3}\) cubic units.

Since \((\vec{c}\times\vec{a})\cdot\vec{b} = [\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{b}]\), and the scalar triple product is unchanged under a cyclic permutation of its vectors, \([\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{b}] = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\).
Also \(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\), and \(\vec{b}\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}) = [\vec{b}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{c}] = -[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) (swapping the first two vectors of a scalar triple product reverses its sign).
So the given expression becomes:
\(\dfrac{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} + \dfrac{-[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]}{[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]} = 1 + (-1) = 0\)
(Since \(\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}\) are non-coplanar, \([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\neq0\), so the division is valid.) — Hence proved.

By the vector triple product identity, \(\vec{b}\times(\vec{c}\times\vec{d}) = (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{d})\vec{c} - (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{d}\)
So \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{c}\times\vec{d}) = \vec{a}\cdot\big[\vec{b}\times(\vec{c}\times\vec{d})\big] = \vec{a}\cdot\big[(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{d})\vec{c}-(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{d}\big]\)
\(= (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{d})(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}) - (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}) = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{d}) - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d})(\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c})\)
This is exactly the expansion of the \(2\times2\) determinant:
\((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{c}\times\vec{d}) = \begin{vmatrix}\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} & \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\\ \vec{a}\cdot\vec{d} & \vec{b}\cdot\vec{d}\end{vmatrix}\) — Hence proved.

Coterminus edges: \(\vec{a}=\hat{j}+\hat{k},\ \vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{k},\ \vec{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}\), i.e. \(\vec{a}=(0,1,1),\vec{b}=(1,0,1),\vec{c}=(1,1,0)\).
\([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = 0(0\times0-1\times1) - 1(1\times0-1\times1) + 1(1\times1-0\times1) = 0+1+1 = 2\)
Volume of parallelepiped \(= |2| = \mathbf{2}\) cubic units.
Volume of tetrahedron \(= \dfrac{1}{6}|[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]| = \dfrac{1}{6}(2) = \mathbf{\dfrac13}\) cubic units.

Write \(\vec{a}+\vec{b},\ \vec{b}+\vec{c},\ \vec{c}+\vec{a}\) as linear combinations of \(\vec{a},\vec{b},\vec{c}\); the coefficient matrix is
\(M=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\ 0&1&1\\ 1&0&1\end{pmatrix}\)
By multilinearity of the scalar triple product, \([\vec{a}+\vec{b}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{c}+\vec{a}] = \det(M)\,[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)
\(\det(M) = 1(1\times1-1\times0) - 1(0\times1-1\times1) + 0(0\times0-1\times1) = 1+1+0 = 2\)
\(\therefore [\vec{a}+\vec{b}\ \ \vec{b}+\vec{c}\ \ \vec{c}+\vec{a}] = 2[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) — Hence proved.

Since \(A,B,C,D\) are coplanar, the vectors \(\vec{AB}=\vec{b}-\vec{a},\ \vec{AC}=\vec{c}-\vec{a},\ \vec{AD}=\vec{d}-\vec{a}\) (measured from \(A\)) are coplanar, so their scalar triple product is zero:
\([\vec{b}-\vec{a}\ \ \vec{c}-\vec{a}\ \ \vec{d}-\vec{a}] = 0\)
Expanding by multilinearity and dropping every term with a repeated \(\vec{a}\) (which vanishes):
\([\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{d}] - [\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{a}] - [\vec{b}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{d}] - [\vec{a}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{d}] = 0\)
Using cyclic invariance \([\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{a}]=[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) and antisymmetry \([\vec{b}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{d}]=-[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{d}]\), \([\vec{a}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{d}]=-[\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{d}]\):
\([\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{d}] - [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] + [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{d}] + [\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{d}] = 0\)
Rearranging:
\([\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{d}] + [\vec{b}\ \vec{c}\ \vec{d}] + [\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{d}] = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) — Hence proved.

\((\vec{a}+\vec{b})\times(\vec{a}+\vec{c}) = \vec{a}\times\vec{a}+\vec{a}\times\vec{c}+\vec{b}\times\vec{a}+\vec{b}\times\vec{c} = \vec{a}\times\vec{c}-\vec{a}\times\vec{b}+\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\)
(since \(\vec{a}\times\vec{a}=\vec{0}\) and \(\vec{b}\times\vec{a}=-\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\))
Dot with \((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})\), using \([\vec{x}\ \vec{x}\ \vec{y}]=0\) to drop repeated-vector terms:
\((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}) = [\vec{b}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{c}] = -[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)
\((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})\cdot(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}) = [\vec{c}\ \vec{a}\ \vec{b}] = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)
\((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\)
So:
\((\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c})\cdot\big[(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\times(\vec{a}+\vec{c})\big] = -[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] - [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] + [\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}] = -[\vec{a}\ \vec{b}\ \vec{c}]\) — Hence proved.
